incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: dedicated-pool-alert - pool=everest-pool-2 node=gpu-07 metric=ecc_errors rate=high — auto-drain initiated
Maya (on-call SRE): acked. I’m on it.
Rafael (runtime): seeing increased retry/error rate for some AegisHealth tenants on everest-pool-2 in the last 5m. Could be KV-cache corruption?
Maya (on-call SRE): checking node now. can someone confirm which tenants are pinned to gpu-07?
Priya (infra): gpu-07 hosts tenant slices: aegis-vpc-1 (enterprise), aegis-analytics, and a few internal canaries.
Leah (Account): tagging me — AegisHealth is an enterprise VPC customer, active on dedicated pool. They are on business support. I’ll prep a short status once we have impact.
Tom (Customer Eng): I’m on standby for any customer-specific mitigations, can coordinate data-plane fallbacks if needed.
Maya (on-call SRE): node is currently in drain state by controller. kubectl shows pods evicting, but some long-running sessions are stuck in RUNNING.
Maya (on-call SRE): running:
```
$ kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-07
-aegis-infer-01 Running 3/3 aegis-vpc-1
-aegis-batcher-02 Terminating 2/3 aegis-analytics
-internal-canary-1 Running 1/1 redwood-canary
```
Maya (on-call SRE): also grabbing dmesg / syslog for ECC messages.
Infra Bot: hardware-alert: gpu-07 ECC_ERR threshold exceeded (raw counter 112 -> kernel oops candidate). Ticket created: HW-78932.
Priya (infra): dmesg snapshot:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679012] Kernel panic trace? ---
[ 12345.679200] ECC error qdepth spike, initiating device reset.
```
Rafael (runtime): looks like real hardware ECC issues. Best short-term is tenant isolation + migration off this node, and a hot-replace with spare node if available.
Maya (on-call SRE): eviction is ~80% complete. Two aegis sessions stuck (inference endpoints). Tom, can we failover those sessions to aegis-standby endpoints?
Tom (Customer Eng): yes — we have warm-standbies in everest-pool-3 for AegisHealth, can route traffic to them. Will need a quick routing flip + cache warmup.
Maya (on-call SRE): doing routing flip now.
Maya (on-call SRE): @Rafael can you confirm compatibility of models to standby? we might need to fallback to quantized variant if exact match not available.
Rafael (runtime): confirmed. model v2.1-compatible quantized variant available on everest-pool-3. Quality delta small for short window. Recommend automatic fallback policy.
Maya (on-call SRE): routing flip executed: aegis endpoints now pointed at everest-pool-3. Monitoring request success & latency.
Maya (on-call SRE): latencies spiked briefly, then normalized. errors for aegis endpoints down from 12% -> 0.3%. :thumbsup:
Leah (Account): drafting customer note: "We detected a hardware fault affecting one node in your dedicated pool; we’ve moved production traffic to a standby and are working on a replacement. No data loss expected." Anything else to add?
Tom (Customer Eng): add that we’re working with infra for a hardware replacement and will provide ETA for node return.
Priya (infra): we have a spare GPU host in the same rack (gpu-spare-11) that’s already pre-provisioned. Requesting hot-replace. Maya, can you confirm drain completed so I can attach the spare?
Maya (on-call SRE): final evictions done. two pods in Terminating had watchdoged to oom/timeout, but sessions failed over. node is safe to decommission.
Priya (infra): performing hot-swap steps: reimage spare -> join pool -> label -> migrate volumes. I’ll run the steps, ETA ~18m.
Priya (infra): commands executing: 
```
$ tfctl decommission node gpu-07 --force
$ tfctl provision node gpu-spare-11 --pool=everest-pool-2 --labels=gpu:v100,zone:us-west2
```
Maya (on-call SRE): plan B if spare fails: move some Aegis shards to dedicated reserved capacity in everest-pool-4 (burst), prioritize critical endpoints only.
Rafael (runtime): enabling aggressive prefix cache warmup on everest-pool-3 to reduce cold-start latency for Aegis.
Maya (on-call SRE): capturing post-incident notes: cause looks hardware ECC spike leading to kernel-level device reset and drain.
Infra Bot: HW ticket HW-78932 updated with replacement node allocation gpu-spare-11.
Leah (Account): customer note ready, sending now. "We routed your traffic to a standby node and are replacing the affected hardware. We'll send an update when replacement completes. Current impact: transient errors resolved, latency back to baseline."
Tom (Customer Eng): I let Aegis SRE know to watch for any anomalies.
Priya (infra): spare joined the pool; provisioning completed. labeling + taints handled. run final sanity checks.
Priya (infra): final health summary: gpu-spare-11 online, all pods scheduled back where policies prefer.
Maya (on-call SRE): validating. I see no residual errors in metrics, per-tenant request error% stable.
Rafael (runtime): running a quick smoke eval on Aegis endpoints — passes perf & quality thresholds.
Maya (on-call SRE): incident status: mitigated -> node replaced, customer traffic restored to dedicated capacity. Logging this thread to postmortem queue.
Leah (Account): sending customer follow-up with ETA for hardware return to service and offering a 1:1 postmortem if they want.
Tom (Customer Eng): will coordinate deeper log share if Aegis requests.
Maya (on-call SRE): handing off to Priya for hardware verification and to Rafael for 2hr follow-up on runtime regressions. If anything new pops, page me (Maya). Handoff note: check nvlink stats, run burn-in on spare for 6 hours.
Priya (infra): ack. I’ll document steps and update HW-78932 with burn-in results.
Rafael (runtime): ack. I’ll watch model quality dashboards for 2 hours and flag any regressions.
Maya (on-call SRE): marking as resolved in pager duty. closing thread in ~30m after attaching logs. nice quick team work :celebrate:
Infra Bot: Incident closed by Maya (on-call SRE) — mitigation complete.
Leah (Account): thanks everyone. I’ll follow up with customer summary email and an optional postmortem meeting.
Tom (Customer Eng): great work.
Maya (on-call SRE): good job team.
